title: Large-Scale Real-Time Notification System Architecture with WebSockets & Redis Pub/Sub
summary: Designing a distributed WebSocket cluster supporting 100,000+ concurrent connections with Redis Adapter and reliable message replay buffer.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.context-problem: When applications scale to hundreds of thousands of concurrent active users, conventional HTTP polling for notifications severely overloads database servers and consumes excessive network bandwidth. The system demands low-latency real-time event delivery below 200ms.
sections.system-requirements:
• Throughput & Concurrency: Maintain 100,000+ concurrent WebSocket connections across a multi-node cluster.
  • Latency & Reliability: Deliver notifications within 200ms with At-Least-Once guarantees and automated client reconnection.
sections.architecture-design:
Distributed WebSocket architecture utilizing Redis Pub/Sub as the central message bus:

  • WebSocket Gateway: Node.js / Go cluster managing stateful socket connections with clients.
  • Redis Pub/Sub Bus: New notifications are published to user-specific channels and broadcast to the specific cluster node holding the connection.
  • Message Replay Buffer: Retain the last 50 messages on Redis Streams to replay missed alerts upon client reconnection.
sections.trade-offs-analysis:
Comparing pure WebSockets versus Server-Sent Events (SSE):

  • SSE: Simpler, runs over HTTP/2, but only supports unidirectional server-to-client streaming.
  • WebSocket: Full-duplex communication requiring stateful connection management, yet uniquely suited for two-way interactive features (presence, typing indicators, acknowledgments).
sections.lessons-best-practices: Always enforce a 30-second Heartbeat / Ping-Pong cycle to prune dead zombie connections, and configure Nginx Load Balancer with proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;.

title: Applying Event Sourcing & CQRS in Stream Processing with Kafka Streams
summary: Guaranteeing immutable financial audit logs and restoring localized State Stores for real-time analytical queries.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.business-data-requirements: In digital banking and payment ledgers, directly updating balances with UPDATE balance = balance + x risks losing critical audit history during dispute reconciliation or concurrency race conditions.
sections.data-modeling:
Event Sourcing models state changes as an append-only stream of immutable facts:

  • Event Log: AccountOpened, MoneyDeposited, and MoneyWithdrawn events are sequenced in Kafka topics partitioned by account_id.
  • Read Model (CQRS): PostgreSQL / Elasticsearch databases hold projections optimized specifically for read-heavy API queries.
sections.pipeline-construction:
Kafka Streams topology architecture:

  • KStream & KTable: Leverage KTable backed by local RocksDB state stores to continuously aggregate balances.
  • Changelog Topic: State Stores continuously synchronize to Kafka Changelog topics for instant disaster recovery upon container failover.
sections.testing-optimization: Stress testing with TopologyTestDriver simulating 50,000 events/sec. Tuned RocksDB block cache allocations and set commit.interval.ms = 100 to minimize disk write amplification.
sections.summary-recommendations: Event Sourcing provides 100% transparent auditability and time-travel debugging capabilities. Recommendation: Implement periodic Snapshotting to avoid prolonged log replay during system warm-up at scale.
